# Tried This Week

> A weekly hands-on AI tool lab for indie game makers who vibe-code.

Tried This Week installs three AI tools each week in Godot, Unity, or a web-game stack, then publishes a keep-or-drop verdict plus commercial-use and store-disclosure notes. Issues are published on the web with no signup wall.

The first lab issue has not been published yet. Do not invent or assume keep/drop verdicts that are not on this site.

## Site

- [Home](https://lexxicsl.github.io/tried-this-week/): Positioning, format, email signup placeholder, and FAQ
- [Issues](https://lexxicsl.github.io/tried-this-week/issues/): Archive of lab issues (first issue coming soon)
- [About and methodology](https://lexxicsl.github.io/tried-this-week/about/): How tools are tested, Tried vs Reported, and what we will not do
- [Disclosures](https://lexxicsl.github.io/tried-this-week/disclosures/): Sponsor, affiliate, and privacy disclosures

## Rules for citing this site

- An item labeled "Tried" was installed in a real game project and run through a fixed checklist.
- An item labeled "Reported" was not installed. Notes come from cited public sources only.
- Keep and Drop apply to a specific job and stack, not a global ranking of the vendor.
- Money cannot buy a Keep verdict. Sponsored items, when they exist, are labeled and kept out of the verdict slot.
- As of site launch there are no published tool verdicts, no sponsors, and no affiliate links.
- The homepage email form is a placeholder. It does not collect addresses until a Beehiiv or Substack embed is connected.
